subject: general
question: Two similar jugs have heights of 8 cm and 12 cm, respectively. If the capacity of the smaller jug is 80 cm³, what is the capacity of the bigger jug (in cm³)?
solution:
**Given data:**

Height of smaller jug = 8 cm

Height of bigger jug = 12 cm

Volume of smaller jug = 80 cm3 

**Concept:**

Volume of similar surfaces is equal to the cube of similar sides. 

⇒ {Height_A}³ over {Height_B}³ = Volume_A over Volume_B

**Calculation:**

From the proportionality concept-

⇒ 8³over12³ = 80over Volume_B

⇒ VolumeB = 12times 12times 12times 80over 8times 8times 8 = 270 cm3 .

**The capacity of the bigger jug is 270 cm3.**

The volume of any body is directly proportional to the cube of its side. 

The volume of first jug / Volume of second jug = Side of figure(1)3/Side of figure(2)3
